$comment: Figma layer path (as in spec.json) -> element inside the entry's target (.ds-memory-panel).

Header/Badge.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font. Figma's 6 px sides are the Badge's 2 px padding plus its label's 4 px in code.

Switch.$why: Switch's own check covers its insides.

Categories.$why: Figma draws the 1 px line under the row as its own layer; in code it is the row's bottom border (39 px).

All.$why: It hugs its label and count, whose widths follow the font; the space between them is a space in code.

Preferences.$why: It hugs its label and count, whose widths follow the font; the space between them is a space in code.

Memories.$why: The list holds all 8 memories and scrolls (listMaxHeight is Figma's height); the frame's own height is checked by the panel's. Off, Figma fades the list to 50 % (its words fall under 4.5:1); code mutes the words instead.

PREFERENCES/Title.$why: The heading spans the list in code; Figma's hugs the word.

PREFERENCES/Memory#1/Badge.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font. Figma's 6 px sides are the Badge's 2 px padding plus its label's 4 px in code.

Editing.$why: Editing, the field has focus: code draws the ring colour and the focus ring, as other in-place fields do; Figma draws the rest stroke (colors/input).

Editing/Button.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font.

Editing/Button#1.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font.

Forgot/Button.$why: It hugs its label, whose width follows the font.

New memory.$why: Figma draws the 1 px line above the row as its own layer; in code it is the row's top border (37 px). Figma's row has no right padding (its words hug); code keeps 16 px so a long label stays clear of the edge.

Footer.$why: Figma draws the 1 px line above the footer as its own layer; in code it is the footer's top border (45 px).
